title: feat(spec,ci): temporal hooks onto the IDataDriver contract; conformance job with live non-UTC servers
body:
Closes the two debts the datetime storage work (#3912/#3942/#3954, PRs #3953/#3964) left open in ADR-0053: **D-A2** (contract promotion) and **D-A3** (conformance backstop).

## D-A2 — the temporal hooks become contract members

`temporalFilterValue` and `temporalFilterColumnSql` — the pair that closed #3912's storage-form drift — were duck-typed: analytics probed `typeof driver.x === 'function'` against a locally-invented `DriverLike`, and nothing at the type level said a driver must implement **both or neither**. #3912's lesson is precisely that coercing the comparand without normalising the column reintroduces half the bug, so a driver implementing one hook alone would silently regress.

Both are now optional members of `IDataDriver` (`spec/contracts/data-driver.ts`), in their own contract section documented as a **pair** with "absent = identity" semantics — a driver whose storage form is the wire form (memory, mongo) simply omits them. Enforcement comes free from what already exists:

- `SqlDriver implements IDataDriver`, so its two signatures are compile-checked from here on.
- Analytics derives its driver seam via `Pick<IDataDriver, …>` instead of a local shape, so the seam cannot drift from the contract. The runtime `typeof` guards remain — that is the correct way to consume an optional contract member.
- `coerceFilterValueForSql` already sits *behind* the hook as the last-resort boolean/number recovery for non-temporal columns — the demotion D-A2 asked for — and stays in exactly that role.

ADR-0053's status line and D-A2 block record the resolution. No runtime behaviour change.

## D-A3 — the live-server suites actually run somewhere

The suites from #3912/#3942 are opt-in (`OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL` / `OS_TEST_MYSQL_URL`) and skip without a server — so nothing ran them in CI, and the seam they guard could regress silently. That gap is exactly what D-A3 warned about.

New **`temporal-conformance`** job in ci.yml, gated on the same `core` paths filter:

- **postgres:16** and **mysql:8.0** service containers. Services cannot override the image command, so the zones are set post-start (`ALTER SYSTEM SET timezone='Asia/Shanghai'` + reload; `SET GLOBAL time_zone='+08:00'`), echoed back for the log.
- **Every timezone is deliberately different**: servers at +08:00, the Node process at `America/New_York`, assertions in UTC. That triangle is what caught every bug in this family; on all-UTC infrastructure they are invisible. Both suites assert they are pointed at a non-UTC server, so a mis-provisioned service fails loudly instead of letting the job pass vacuously.
- The **whole** driver-sql suite runs under the skewed process zone — not just the live-server files — so a TZ-sensitive assumption anywhere in the driver's tests fails here before it ships.
- `mysql:8.0` also covers the other half of the #3942 compatibility claim: the hands-on verification ran on MariaDB 10.11, the stricter dialect for datetime literals.
- MySQL health check pings over TCP (`-h 127.0.0.1`) because the image's init phase runs with networking disabled — a socket ping reports healthy before init finishes.

## Verification

- The exact CI command was run locally against a live PG 16 (`TimeZone=Asia/Shanghai`) and MariaDB (`+08:00`) with `TZ=America/New_York`: **47 files, 480/480, zero skips** — both live suites activated.
- `pnpm build` + `pnpm test` green (132 tasks); spec doc gates (`check:docs` / `check:skill-refs` / `check:react-blocks`) green.
- YAML validated.

## Note for review

The first run of the new job on this very PR is its own end-to-end test — if the service provisioning or the timezone bootstrap is wrong, the suites' non-UTC guards will say so explicitly rather than skipping.
